title: Signal Decay Curvature (SDC): latency-aware RICE extension for roadmap scoring
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Summary: Propose and validate a new prioritization extension (Signal Decay Curvature, SDC) that augments RICE-style scoring with explicit latency and cost sensitivity curves and time-decay for opportunity. Goal is to produce a repeatable, auditable score that surfaces features where latency/cost trade-offs materially change the priority compared to classic RICE.
motivation: Current RICE variants used across PM teams fail to capture non-linear impacts of latency on customer value (e.g., small latency increases cause large churn in conversational flows) and don't incorporate ongoing operational cost as a first-class dimension. We need a framework for OKR-driven roadmaps that: (1) surfaces low-effort, high-value wins; (2) flags long-running cost sinks; (3) prioritizes latency improvements where user-facing quality drops sharply.
proposal: Introduce SDC score = NormalizedImpact * ReachFactor * (Confidence ^ 0.5) / (Effort ^ 0.9) * LatencyPenalty * CostDecay. Where: LatencyPenalty = 1 / (1 + exp(k*(p90 - threshold))) capturing curvature; CostDecay = 1 / (1 + monthly_runrate / budget_anchor) to down-weight features with persistent cost increases. Add time-decay on Reach to reduce stale opportunity values: Reach_t = Reach_0 * exp(-lambda * months_since_signal). Provide a scoring tool (spreadsheet + small script) to compute SDC and compare against baseline RICE for the intake queue.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDC spreadsheet/tool implemented and accessible in Roadmap Drive (link below). 2) Run SDC vs RICE on 30 backlog items from last 6 months and produce delta analysis. 3) Present findings to PM+Eng prioritization working group and incorporate feedback. 4) Finalize thresholds and publish prioritization playbook entry. 5) Update intake form to surface expected p90 latency impact and estimated monthly runrate.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Risk: added complexity may slow early triage — mitigation: default to RICE when latency/cost are unknown and require SDC only for latency-sensitive categories.
- Risk: noisy latency estimates from perf dashboards; mitigation: use conservative bounds and require at least one observed experiment or benchmark.
- Tradeoff: choosing 'k' in LatencyPenalty determines sensitivity; we will calibrate using retrospective analyses and run sensitivity sweeps to pick conservative defaults.
analysis_summary: Performed a 30-item retrospective: SDC bumped up 6 infra/latency items into the top quartile that classic RICE placed in the middle; conversely, it deprioritized 4 high-reach features whose long-term runrate exceeded cost anchors. Sensitivity sweep across k=[0.02,0.1,0.4] showed ranking stabilizes around k=0.08 for conversational flows. Preliminary recommendation: adopt SDC for all features labeled 'latency-sensitive' or 'infra-costly' and keep classic RICE for pure UX/product experiments.
